title: Shifted free graded modules sheafify to twists
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. For every integer $d$, the associated sheaf $\widetilde{S(d)}$ of the graded shift $S(d)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] is isomorphic to the twisting module $\mathcal O_P(d)$ defined by the standard affine cover of [def-sc-p1-standard] and [lem-sc-p1-twist-exists]; consequently the associated sheaf of a finite direct sum of shifts is the corresponding finite direct sum of twists.

proof.text: Prove that the two variable basic opens cover polynomial Proj using Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' and MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X_eq_top, then lift the index from Fin 2 to ULift(Fin 2). Apply [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-projection-chart-iso] on both target standard opens; by Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.iff_of_iSup_eq_top for isomorphisms, the canonical linear projection is an isomorphism. Take its asIso. Its chart equations are awayι_linearProjection, so it defines the required ProjChartIsomorphism C.

Choose a glued module L and its TwistData T by [lem-sc-p1-twist-exists]. For the constructed C and this particular L,T, apply [lem-sc-p1-proj-twist-glued-comparison] to obtain the comparison iso. Package T as Nonempty and pair these witnesses; invertibility and uniqueness supplied by the existence theorem are unnecessary for the present conclusion.

For each finite family a, specialize [lem-sc-proj-finite-twist-coproduct-fractions] to A=k[x₀,x₁] with its homogeneousSubmodule grading. This provides exactly the additive injections, ranges, scalar formulas and canonical restriction formulas required by the second conjunct. Combine the two conjuncts under the same C.
